HUD is well aware of the problems of such housing for families, and is conducting research on these problems outside of Operation BREAKTHROUGH.
Comment: How will future private developments be controlled?
Response: HUD requires appropriate Environmental Statements to be filed for any Federally-assisted project and provides evaluation and approval for such projects. The BREAKTHROUGH sites are intended as demonstrations of the value of careful planning.
Comment: Impact on mineral industries.
Response: The final statement discusses the need to supplement existing material supplies used in construction, by development of alternatives or supplemental supplies. The questions of zoning and other policies which could impact development of such resources are noted, but not appropriately addressed within BREAKTHROUGH. Final decisions as to material utilization will depend on availability, cost, market decisions, and acceptance. BREAKTHROUGH is working to improve the last three of these.
Comment: Prior attempts to utilize new materials.
Response: This comment cites the "Lustron" home as possibly being rejected due to sociological or environmental problems. Many Lustron homes are still being occupied as acceptable housing; the failure of the corporation was due to financial problems more than to design. It does not seem appropriate to discuss this type of history in the statement.
Comment: Use of solid waste material in housing construction.
Response: This comment is welcome as an area for future investigation. No housing system selected for BREAKTHROUGH proposed such utilization.
Comment: Format is incorrect.
Response: Correction has been made in final statement.
D. Department of the Army
<u>Comment</u>: Relationship of industrialized housing to conventional communities.
Response: The final statement discusses the care taken in site planning and system design to provide this harmony. Note that the system designs generally attempt to meet conventional standards for good design.
